issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a no-argument constructor (students are instructed to implement a no-arg constructor and Main uses new Farm()). However, the solution implements only a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor and does not provide a no-argument constructor. This mismatch can confuse students and cause tests or example code that call new Farm() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor for Farm in the solution (and/or template) that initializes the animals list, for example: public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to explicitly require and use a constructor with an initialCapacity parameter, and change uses of new Farm() accordingly.
